source: AMK KW26-S5-FSE-4Q manual, PDK_205481 (version 2017/02), section 8.1.3 'Data telegrams' (pp. 60-62) and 8.2.4 'Units' (p. 65). Each telegram is 8 bytes, Intel byte order. The inverter sends every ID34028 'BUS output rate' (default 5 ms) and reads setpoints every 1 ms; with no setpoint telegram for more than 50 ms it faults and coasts (setpoint 0 %MN). IDs are base address + node address (ID34023 'BUS address participant'), which must be chosen so no two COB-IDs on a bus are the same: AV1 at node n is 0x282+n and AV2 is 0x284+n, so nodes 1, 2, 5, 6 (not 3, 4). Cross-checked against HyTech's HT_CAN (INV1..4, the same fields re-packed under their own IDs).

actual_values_1.comment: AMK Actual Values 1 (base 0x282): status word and actual values

signals.name: torque_current
signals.comment: AMK_TorqueCurrent: raw torque current Iq, relative to ID110 'Converter peak current' (manual 8.2.4; its formula is a figure)

signals.name: magnetizing_current
signals.comment: AMK_MagnetizingCurrent: raw magnetizing current Id, relative to ID110 'Converter peak current' (manual 8.2.4)

actual_values_2.comment: AMK Actual Values 2 (base 0x284): temperatures and diagnostic number

setpoints_1.comment: AMK Setpoints 1 (base 0x183): control word and setpoints. Torque control is speed control with torque limits (ID32800 = 0x480003): a setpoint far above the motor's speed with the positive limit at the torque wanted, or 0 rpm with the negative limit for regen

signals.name: error_reset
signals.comment: AMK_bErrorReset: remove error (only with every setpoint 0)

signals.name: torque_limit_positive
signals.comment: AMK_TorqueLimitPositiv: positive torque limit, of the motor's nominal torque MN (ID32771)

signals.name: torque_limit_negative
signals.comment: AMK_TorqueLimitNegativ: negative torque limit, of the motor's nominal torque MN (ID32771)
